citation: Ghostty's own defaults, which Muster matches wherever Ghostty has an answer: cmd+d and cmd+shift+d for splits, cmd+w to close, cmd+[ and cmd+] to step, cmd+opt+arrow to select a neighbour, cmd+t for a tab. The two Ghostty has no answer for are ours: resize on cmd+ctrl+shift+arrow, and zoom on cmd+shift+return.
why: Somebody arriving from the terminal Muster embeds should not have to learn a second set of chords for the same actions, and a default that quietly drifts from Ghostty's is worse than one that never matched - it works everywhere except the one place muscle memory sends it. The two Muster invents follow the pattern rather than filling gaps at random: resize is focus with one more finger, so moving to a pane and growing it are the same hand position and a mistyped focus cannot resize. This is the policy half of Stage 3; what a shell does with these is its own, and turning a chord into a menu item is pinned in the shell's tests.

cases.name: the splits, on Ghostty's own chords
cases.why: The pair somebody presses most, and the pair where a wrong modifier is least visible: cmd+d and cmd+shift+d differ by one key and produce arrangements that both look plausible.

cases.name: making a tab and closing a pane
cases.why: Both are chords the platform already means something by, so a default has to be the one people expect rather than a free choice.

cases.name: stepping through panes in order
cases.why: The two that reach every pane whatever shape the tab is in, which is why they are bound to something reachable one-handed rather than to arrows.

cases.name: selecting the neighbour in a direction
cases.why: Ergonomics rather than reachability - next and previous already reach everything - so these are the ones a hand rests on, and they carry one modifier fewer than resize.

cases.name: resize is focus with one more finger
cases.why: The relationship is the design: moving to a pane and growing it are the same hand position, and a mistyped focus cannot resize. Ghostty has no default here, so this is ours to keep consistent.

cases.name: zoom
cases.why: The one that matters at fifteen panes: read a pane properly and press it again to have the arrangement back. Return because it is the key nothing else in this set uses and it is under the same hand as the modifiers.

cases.name: showing the agents, on the chord the platform uses for a list
cases.why: The one default that does not come from Ghostty, because Ghostty has no sidebar. Cmd+B is where a Mac app with a list down the side puts it, and no terminal wants the chord: a command chord is a menu key equivalent on this platform and never reaches a pane. It is a window action rather than a pane action, which is why it sits at the end of the list rather than among the splits - a menu is read top to bottom and this is not part of arranging panes.

cases.name: the list of shortcuts is itself an action with a shortcut
cases.why: It is a window action like the rest, which is what makes it rebindable and what puts it in its own list. Cmd+/ is where a list of shortcuts lives in most things that have one, and nothing in a terminal wants the chord.

cases.name: every action has one, and no two share a chord
cases.why: An action with no default is one nobody can reach without editing a config file, and two on the same chord is one of them silently never firing - which on macOS shows up as a menu item that looks bound and does nothing.
